paper.title_en: Reactive feedback for suppression of the periodic transient beam loading effect in storage rings: theory and simulations
paper.abstract_en: In fourth-generation synchrotron light sources, harmonic cavities are often employed for bunch lengthening. The reduced longitudinal focusing, combined with high total $R/Q$ of these cavities, can make the beam susceptible to the periodic transient beam loading (PTBL) effect, a multibunch instability characterized by slow oscillations in bunch centroids and lengths and by its resistance to conventional feedback damping. In this work, building on a recent proposal of applying reactive feedback to control the PTBL effect, we developed a frequency-domain theoretical model, including the feedback voltage in the linearized Vlasov equation to derive a Lebedev equation modified by the feedback transfer function. The reactive feedback was also implemented in the time domain in the macroparticle tracking code \texttt{STABLE}. The methods were applied to the parameters of the double-rf system of the MAX IV storage ring. Both approaches show that, above a threshold gain, an idealized pure reactive feedback is able to suppress the PTBL effect, with good agreement between theory and simulations across beam currents and $R/Q$ values. Realistic hardware limitations were included in the analysis, determining the limits for feedback gain, latency, and bandwidth, which are compatible with existing bunch-by-bunch feedback systems. Using the HALF storage ring parameters, the semi-analytical results indicate that the reactive feedback can be extended to suppress the PTBL effect in triple-rf systems, albeit at higher threshold gains than for double-rf systems.
